title: Automatic differentiation is confidently wrong
summary: Pathwise AAD differentiates a cash-or-nothing digital payoff to exactly zero almost everywhere and emits no error, even though the analytic delta is material.
trigger: Differentiate a sharp at-the-money digital call pathwise using the same Monte Carlo normals as the price estimator.
observed: AAD returns 0.000000 against a true delta of 0.019333, while a crude central difference is correct within 0.1 percent.
invariant: A derivative method must match the regularity of the payoff; a finite price does not imply a valid pathwise derivative.
fix: Replace the step with a call-spread smoothing choice, then report the bias-versus-variance trade instead of calling smoothing exact.

timeline.title: Differentiate the step
timeline.detail: Every sampled payoff follows a locally flat branch except on a measure-zero strike boundary.

timeline.title: Reverse-sweep zero
timeline.detail: The tape behaves exactly as implemented and propagates a zero adjoint without a warning.

timeline.title: Compare with the analytic Greek
timeline.detail: The test proves the true delta exceeds 0.015 and central difference recovers it.

timeline.title: Choose smoothing explicitly
timeline.detail: A width-one call spread recovers the delta within five percent while exposing the modeling choice.

limits: Smoothing introduces bias and is a modeling choice, not a universal repair for discontinuous payoffs.
